desc:
The bitwise OR of a subarray is the OR of all its elements (for a single element it is the element itself). Given an array nums of non-negative integers and a number k, return the length of the shortest non-empty subarray whose OR is greater than or equal to k, or -1 if there is none.

nums = [2, 1, 8], k = 10
[2, 1] -> 3, [1, 8] -> 9, [2, 1, 8] -> 11
result = 3
hints: Adding an element to a window can only turn bits on, so the OR of a window never decreases when the window grows. That makes two pointers possible.
The difficulty is removing the left element: you cannot 'un-OR' a value. What extra information would let you know whether a bit is still set after a removal?
Keep a counter for each of the 30 bit positions: how many elements of the window have that bit set. A bit is on in the window's OR exactly when its counter is positive.
editorial: OR is monotone under extension, so for every right end the valid left ends form a prefix, and the best left end only moves right. A sliding window fits, but OR has no inverse operation. The fix is to store, for each bit, how many window elements contain it.

Adding x increments the counter of every set bit of x; removing it decrements them. The window's OR is rebuilt from the counters (a bit is set when its counter is positive), and we update it incrementally as counters go from 0 to 1 or 1 to 0. For each right end, shrink while the OR is still at least k and record the length. Each element is added and removed once with 30 bit operations each: O(30 n) time and O(30) space. Note that k = 0 is satisfied by any single element, so the answer is 1.
